object_description: compact rotated cross-shaped volume with mezzanines
design_condition: The building rotates slightly from the orthogonal structure to align with the street, turns its entrance toward the site center, and uses mezzanines to respond to the topography while forming open spaces on both sides.

positive.statement: The proposal impresses with its precise analysis of the site and its sensitive response to the existing structure.

position.rationale: Site-sensitive placement is approximated at the lower-western building and terrain interface.

positive.statement: The rotated setting creates an address and makes well-proportioned open spaces possible.

position.rationale: Rotated footprint and flanking open spaces are clearly legible in the top view.

positive.statement: The route through the site is logical and attractive.

position.rationale: The likely site route is anchored along the western and southern approach.

positive.statement: The clear organization enables an elegant and coherent constructive logic.

position.rationale: Overall organization and stacked construction are visible across plan and elevations.

positive.statement: The mezzanine floors create an attractive and versatile learning landscape that inspires.

position.rationale: Split-level floor bands are visible through the stepped elevation profiles.

positive.statement: Classrooms, group rooms, anterooms, and stairs can be connected in varied ways while remaining clearly articulated.

position.target: classrooms, group rooms, anterooms, and stairs
position.rationale: Interior functions are not separable, so the central upper building surface is used as an anchor.

positive.statement: The project is consistently thought through as a site-specific, innovative, and surprising typology.

position.rationale: The unusual rotated cross-shaped mass is visible in plan and elevations.

positive.statement: The interplay of setting, accessibility, and outdoor areas creates differentiated and coherent lounge spaces.

position.rationale: Differentiated outdoor-facing zones are approximated beside the eastern building edge.

positive.statement: The different play areas form a coherent whole through their individual orientations and planting.

position.rationale: Play areas are not individually identifiable, so a distributed upper-eastern site anchor is used.

negative.statement: The entrance to the site is cramped and unclearly cut into the terrain.

position.rationale: The entrance is anchored at the cramped lower-western site edge.

negative.statement: The kindergarten is partially oriented toward the street, and the western outdoor space is low.

position.rationale: Street-oriented kindergarten and low western open space are approximated along the west side.

negative.statement: A ball guard would be needed opposite the entrance.

position.rationale: The safety element is placed opposite the western entrance approach.

negative.statement: The western path connection in combination with the split level and topography is not convincing.

position.rationale: The criticized connection is localized along the western path and split-level edge.

negative.statement: The cut in the terrain between the grass playing field and the lower kindergarten access is unfortunate.

position.target: terrain cut between playing field and kindergarten access
position.rationale: The terrain transition is approximated between the southern play zone and lower access.

negative.statement: The split-level organization is convincing spatially but appears forced in the terrain and is not technically complete.

position.rationale: Split levels are visible in the stepped massing, though technical completeness is not measurable.

negative.statement: The stairwell must be closed for fire safety if the building is extended, obscuring the basic idea of the design.

position.rationale: The stairwell is approximated within the upper central circulation band.
